text: So you arrived in, uh, at, uh, in the Scuderia in 1999 after the accident of Michael J- uh, Schumacher in Silverstone. Uh, how did it happen exactly? Uh, you have a call? Uh, can you tell us the story of, of this moment? Yeah, it's, um, I was, I was actually in Silverstone for, I think it was Friday practice, and I went back to Finland and, uh, on Sunday morning, and, uh, I saw Michael's accident on TV in the airport. And, uh, I didn't think much of it and, uh, because it didn't look big, so I, I was just hoping he's fine. And, uh, then, uh, couple hours later, I heard he broke his leg and, uh, didn't think anything. So, uh, I was getting married during the n- next week. We had a, like, a wedding rehearsal on Monday, and then I had a phone call from Jean Todt. Aye, yi, yi. And, uh, he called me when we were practicing this, uh, wedding and, uh, and, um, he said, uh, "I want you to come to Maranello." And I thought, "Oh, okay." Uh, I kn- of course, immediately I can connect these two things. And, uh, he, uh... I asked, "When?" He said, "Now." So he did n- not give me option. I said, "I'm my we- I'm in my wedding re- rehearsal." And he said, "It doesn't matter. You come to Maranello now." Yeah, it was, Ferrari was very kind to me when I went there. It was, I felt very welcome from day one. We had a really good time of staying in Jean's house in Maranello. And, uh, Jean, Jean is like a workaholic. He works nonstop. Uh, he sleeps, like, two hours a night, and then he's works all the other time, so I never saw him. And, uh, I was getting very hungry in his house because there was no food, so, uh, Ross Brawn brought me some food in the evening to eat and, uh... But, uh, I felt so welcomed from beginning and, uh, every time I went to factory and everybody was helping me, and I had phone calls with Michael also, and Michael helped me how to adapt in the team quickly, quickly and because next race was already one week later. So he was supportive on this time to, to help you to find- Yes ... the best way to adapt to the car. I, I talked a lot with Michael on the phone and, uh, we had video calls and, uh, and, uh, he was helping me a lot, um, to teach me about the people in the team who I need to go if I need something specific for the car. So he told me the names which, uh, who I need to talk and, uh, it just, uh, it, it was very, very easy to adapt. And of course, I knew Eddie from before also, so it was quite easy, easy to get help from him also. And you, you were quickly competitive because some, uh, weeks a- after that in Germany, you were close to, to win. I had, uh, Heinz-Harald Frentzen behind me. I s- it was yellow car. I was all the time hoping, "Yes, stay there, stay there." And then Eddie managed to pass Heinz during pit stops, and then I saw red car behind me and I thought, "Oh, okay. And now I know what's gonna happen next." And then very soon came the radio call from Ross Brawn with his calm voice that, "Mika, I want you to let Eddie pass this lap." Yeah. And you sacrificed your- [coughs] Excuse me. And you f- sacrificed your first victory for, for the, the happiness of the Scuderia and of also for the giving the maximum chance for Eddie Irvine. Uh, uh, you have a, a special relationship with, uh, with, uh, Michael Schumacher on this time. We, um, like a fan, uh, we, uh, we have the vision of a, a driver who is very, uh, implicated in, uh, very serious in, in his jobs. And all people we met today in Mugello said he was a, a so kind driver, so kind a gentleman in the life. Yeah, he was nice guy. We, we knew each other from karting already, and we used to race karting. We did, uh, Formula Ford together. Actually, I beat him in Formula Ford quite, mm, I fin- I won the European Championship, but Michael finished second. And, uh, Formula 3, we were, uh, Macau Grand Prix, Michael won, I was second, and Eddie third. [chuckles] So it's, we, we've been, we've been growing up- It's a long story between you and- We've been growing up together, so I know him from a long time. Yeah. And, uh, after this, uh, experience, you have a, um, a vision different of Formula 1 because it was maybe the, the most important, uh, uh, team, uh, for who you drive on this time. I know you, you have, you have experiences with, uh, with, uh, Toyota, you experiences with Zacro. Uh, but it was a, uh, different strategy, different organization. It's a big, big factory. It's really a, a different culture, DNA in the Ferrari. Yeah. It was my first, like, big team. I was in Tyrrell and Arrows and, uh, smaller teams before. So it was first, like, a big team and, uh, of course, it opened my eyes for many things. Uh, how quick they can react for if we need something for the car and, uh, they would do it immediately, not think about it for two weeks, and, uh, it was in the car immediately, and the factory was working nonstop and, uh, the resources they have, and we were testing so much. We had a different test team waiting every time after the race. We went to different circuits, and there was a test team waiting and, uh, so many laps and so much testing. Sometimes I got a call in the middle of the night in Maranello, and, uh, some engineer found something in the dampers. So I went, the middle of the night they woke me up and, "Come here." I went there and did three laps over the curbs. And, uh, this experience for Ferrari, I, I, I believe was, uh, wonderful for you because it gave you a, a, a great, um, exposition, worldwide exposition with your amazing results. It was a chance for you to, to, to go to Toyota behind. It's Ferrari who give you this opportunity to go to Toyota? Yeah, it, uh, sort of, I went to Sauber first because it had a Ferrari engine. So, uh, John wanted to put me in, uh, Sauber to stay in the family kind of. But then, uh, Toyota came up after that and, uh, Toyota's, uh, like, uh, my chance to get in another big team. Only problem Toyota had, uh, Ange Pasquale, he was, uh, only problem with the Toyota, but- Yeah. No, it's a joke. [laughs] Yeah, I know. No. We say hello to, to, uh- Hello, Ange. [laughs] ... to Ange. Yeah. So thank you, Mika, for this interview and, uh, I hope we can make a, a big show with you when you have a moment with us. Thank you very much. Bye-bye. Thank you.
